newsitem.title: USA: CITGO Texas plant fire under control, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: CITGO Texas plant fire under control, no injuries.

text.p: A fire that followed a blast at Citgo Petroleum Corp's Corpus Christi, Texas, refinery is under control and will be allowed to burn out, local emergency services officials said Tuesday.
The blast occured at 2222 CST/2322 EDT/0322 GMT Monday and rocked the local community.
Captain Richard Lewinsky said the fire would probably take between 24 and 48 hours to burn out.

A spokesperson for the plant, Chuck Casales, confirmed that the blast occurred in one of the plant's process units, but he declined to provide further details. The refinery has a rated capacity to process 132,500 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil.
The cause of the explosion is still under investigation, local fire officials said.

"It is under investigation how it started. We didn't have any injuries. One of the private fire company employees was transferred to hospital for observation but that's it," said R.K. Gibson, assistant fire chief at Corpus Christi.

Gibson said it wasn't clear if the explosion was weather-related. "I had just gone to bed and it jarred the station really heavy. At first I thought it was a very loud clap of thunder but it was way to loud for that."
Neither CITGO nor the officials had an estimate of damage.
CITGO is a subsidiary of PDV America Inc, itself a division of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela.
